blocks.text: Ezekiel 27 is a lamentation over Tyre forming part of the extended Tyre cycle in Ezekiel 26-28. This cycle employs varied symbolic imagery—siege and destruction (chapter 26), ship and maritime commerce (chapter 27), garden and precious stones (chapter 28), and the figure of a cherub—to address the historical city of Tyre and its rulers. This approach focuses on the historical city and its rulers rather than explicitly naming Satan. Chapter 27 develops the ship metaphor throughout, using maritime and commercial imagery as the primary vehicle for addressing Tyre.

The text of Ezekiel 27 is preserved in multiple manuscript traditions: the Masoretic Hebrew text, the Old Greek translation (Iezekiel), Papyrus 967 (Greek), Qumran fragments, and the Masada scroll. These witnesses exhibit variation in wording and word order that requires passage-level textual analysis for establishing the most reliable reading.
